title: BCA/19/2024 of TIRATH PRAKASH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Bail Cancellation Application No. 19 of 2024
Shri Tirath Prakash ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Subhash Chand Burman, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, AGA with Mr. Himanshu Sain, Brief
Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The respondent no. 2 is an accused in Case
Crime No. 543 of 2024, under Sections 304 IPC and Section
3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Police Station
Bhagwanpur, District Haridwar ("the case"). He was granted
bail on 14.10.2024 by the court of Sessions Judge,
Haridwar. The applicant is an informant in the case. He has
filed the bail cancellation application for cancellation of bail
granted to the respondent no. 2 ("the accused").
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit
that the bail has been granted to the accused on the
assumption that the incident was an accident, whereas, it is
argued that the deceased was killed by the accused, which
was revealed by CCTV footages. Therefore, it is argued that

2
the bail granted to the accused deserves to be cancelled.
Learned counsel for the applicant would also submit that
one of the friends of the deceased has also filed an affidavit
to the effect that he was told by the deceased that he was
assaulted by the accused.
4. Learned State Counsel would submit that there
is no infirmity in the impugned bail order.
5. In fact, the FIR itself records that a danda or
road was inserted into the anus of the deceased, due to
which he sustained fatal injury. This fact was within the
notice of the court, when the impugned bail order was
passed.
6. The grounds for cancellation of bail are different
than the grounds, which weigh in the mind of the court
while considering the bail application. There should be
strong ground to curtail the liberty once granted to an
accused by way of concession to bail. In the impugned bail
order, the court has taken notice of every fact and also the
fact that the deceased and the applicant both were studying
together in a room and there was no dispute between them.
The court has also taken note of the fact that till his death
on 03.07.2024, the deceased did not lodge any complaint.

3
The incident allegedly took place in a birthday party on
28.06.2024.
7. Having considered the entirety of facts, this
Court is of the view that there is no ground to cancel the bail
granted to the accused. Accordingly, the bail cancellation
application deserves to be rejected.
8. The bail cancellation application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
 17.12.2024
Avneet/
